scene_guidance.display_distance_order: Authored-anchor distance minus subtype offset; clamp to zero; round to whole meters. Display-lifted XYZ never changes distance or range selection.
scene_guidance.mini_game_identity: SceneMarker carries explicit None/Fly/Mole/Wave subtype; reward TreasureMiniGame remains a Treasure and never receives the Mole-only correction.
scene_guidance.focus_validity: Only currently displayed eligible targets. Acquired Aim target may remain inside a 1.2-times exit ellipse. Hidden/removed targets lose labels immediately; valid incumbents retain their label during replacement dwell.
scene_guidance.zero_policy: A zero range or marker limit hides Scene; distance Off hides labels only.
scene_guidance.engine_boundary: Scene projection runs once on every existing EngineTickPost callback outside the shared 16 ms player-position cadence gate. The existing full-catalog nearest selection remains at 250 ms. Each frame refreshes actual distance and validity only for the already selected list of at most 50 markers in linear time, preserving its order instead of sorting again.
scene_guidance.rendering_cost_policy: Scene updates every existing EngineTickPost frame. Eight or more selected markers use five engine calibration points checking both depth axes, plus one actual retained-marker witness within a radial 0.25 physical-pixel tolerance. Calibration is frame-local; no previous camera pose is reused or interpolated. Unsupported, orthographic, missing-camera or mismatched calibration uses native per-marker projection. Exceptional engine faults retain the existing Scene isolation path. Moving groups use volatile painting and disable pixel snapping when the reflected engine enum is available. Every changed subpixel render translation is submitted; unchanged positions reuse state. Edge margins are 52 pixels for new / 44 for retained markers, overlap spacing 40 / 32. Catalog selection remains 250 ms and selected-distance refresh is bounded to 50 points. No measured FPS or latency improvement is claimed.
scene_guidance.f6_preview_policy: F6-owned cursor preview is limited to the settings Hub actually owning its input mode and the native HUD remaining visible. Scene may preview current settings while that owned menu is open; the existing enable, readiness, world/travel, activity, native-menu and HUD guards remain authoritative. Other cursor ownership never grants this exception. Scene creates no new input hook.

predeployment_build_snapshot.scope: SG16 adds independent All controls for Radar and Map, live open-map settings preview with bounded 100 ms coalescing and immediate all-off, Auto focus public defaults, 100 ms initial Aim acquisition with existing 350/500 ms replacement stability, and a compact two-column localized Guide with precise mini-game reward terminology, complete Radar height states, game clock help, aligned Scene legends and four distance rows.

runtime_boundary: Native UMG only; no external executable, Lua renderer, motion bridge, diagnostic shared mapping, or connected PostRender/Present canary.
encounter_discovery_policy: One fixed weak slot per immutable Boss/Assault catalog entry is populated by the UObject creation listener. The existing 250 ms service walks all 49 slots round-robin, resolves the current exact-class Actor position before applying the 100-metre player-to-actor bound, and performs at most eight Actor-position queries per control tick. The observation refreshes its retained numeric position from that live actor instead of treating the static catalog coordinate as the actor position. Travel clears all 49 slots; F8/F7 preserves only valid same-world candidates. No FindAllOf, static catalog-distance prefilter, dynamic encounter queue, file polling, or 16 ms encounter work remains.
encounter_completion_policy: Ordinary disappearance arms after at least four present samples spanning at least one real second, then requires at least forty consecutive missing samples spanning at least ten real seconds while the player remains within 100 metres of the last actual actor position. A visible already-observed RemovedFromWorld edge may start, but never complete, that same missing window when a short Assault ended before ordinary arming. The ended weak UObject is cleared immediately. A cursor-owning map cannot erase this numeric-only ended evidence, although it still invalidates ordinary live weak-pointer disappearance. Unobserved removal, player departure, activity suppression, travel, unavailable state, invalid position, and a returned actor reject or reset missing evidence. Strict exact-class Destroyed EndPlay is the only immediate recovery path and still requires current availability plus bounded actor/catalog/player proximity.
encounter_availability_policy: The ordinary disappearance and strict Destroyed fallbacks pass the current time-window and future-cooldown gates at their final write. Exact NetMulticastNotifyDeath and schema-validated NetMulticastSetDeathProcess End events pass current availability before publishing a catalog bit; ordinary consumption does not recheck that accepted event's time window. A live actor return clears the missing sequence and requests only the existing compact rebind; effective availability changes reuse the existing fixed 49-bit visibility edge and deferred next-map-session atlas policy.
encounter_death_handoff_policy: An accepted exact NotifyDeath or DeathProcess End event sets one bit in one of two fixed 49-bit atomic masks. Ordinary consumption runs only in the existing 250 ms control service and requires enabled, non-transitioning, non-suppressed context with valid player position. Successful or deduplicated application clears that bit from both masks; an apply exception retains it without erasing unrelated or newly published bits. F7, disable, travel, and activity-suppression boundaries may settle pending cooldown and eligibility numerically without renderer mutation before reset. Only safe live-GameThread finalization and the TitleMap owner boundary may hard-clear the masks. True process teardown closes ingress and returns; UObjectArray shutdown does not clear them. No new poll, timer, scan, SQL query, dynamic queue, or steady work is introduced.
world_map_runtime_delta_policy: Rebuild in the current session only when the exact retained DLayerMap attachment is visibly open. An attached but hidden layer is retired and defers atlas work until the next exact SetWorldMapImage event. The matching serviced candidate serial may rearm the bounded three-attempt readiness budget once per layer, including after three early map_id probes exhausted before the renderer published a retryable failure; repeated same-layer delivery cannot replenish work after that one rearm.
compact_viewport_reflow_policy: Compact Radar retains its one-hertz viewport/clock layout service. F6 settings reflow is separate and checks its viewport every 250 ms only while open.
compact_menu_suppression_policy: The exact DLayerMap SetWorldMapImage event latches compact suppression for controller or keyboard navigation. A validated GameplayStatics IsGamePaused sample shares the existing 250 ms activity edge, and the map layer IsVisible property is read only during bounded catch-up or while the latch is active. No controller mapping is read, no timer or scan is added, and the 16 ms motion path reads Boolean suppression state only.
world_map_projection_anchor: The exact current game-native icon Canvas owns two Mod-created hit-test-invisible atlas hosts. Each outer Canvas slot and inner Panel_Point slot is full-stretch with zero offsets; only each locally sized 2048 Image Canvas slot owns the attach-time atlas left, top, width, and height, and Image RenderTranslation remains zero. PlayerIconWidget is read only during a fresh attachment to author that parent-coordinate-space placement. A retained refresh never observes PlayerIcon and reads only the exact FogAbovePanel local extent. When weak parent identity and extent are unchanged, the Image slots remain immutable and refresh performs no layout, transform, visibility, widget-tree, or Retainer mutation. Parent replacement or two-sample stable same-parent extent drift reports RebuildRequired; Main may schedule at most one fresh bounded attachment per open-map session. Initial attach and rebuild each retain an independent three-attempt readiness budget. No AddToViewport host, desktop-resolution input, centered fallback, new poll, per-frame projection path, authored 3000/8000 geometry, or dynamic PlayerIcon rebase is published.

save_callback_limits.failure_policy: Every SQLite C callback contains C++ exceptions and fails the one-shot reconciliation closed on malformed, excessive, or allocation-failing input.

runtime_task_class_mapping.attempt_policy: one post-stability attempt and one delayed retry only after initial failure; success or the second failure stops work; completed travel may start a fresh bounded capture; an already-active explicit F7 rearms only failed capture and preserves completion bits, revisions, and reactivation latches
runtime_task_class_mapping.suppression_policy: confirmed non-open-world activity defers pending capture until open-world rendering resumes
runtime_task_class_mapping.retention: copied class-name strings and catalog indices only
runtime_task_class_mapping.failure_policy: classes used only outside the 147-entry catalog are ignored; a class shared by catalog and non-catalog IDs is ambiguous; missing schema, ambiguous class IDs, duplicate catalog coverage, incomplete coverage, and unmapped callbacks fail closed
runtime_task_class_mapping.completion_race_policy: exact completion increments a fixed per-task revision and clears its reactivation latch; stale scans and later still-active current scans preserve completion; current NONE or END arms reactivation, and only a later current ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS sample restores a repeatable task and starts a new task generation; FAIL does not arm. Three non-confirming save attempts lock the current generation against repeated-event replenishment; only that two-scan reactivation or a new F7 unlocks it. InitGameState pre-transition drains any already published exact bits into numeric completion and prerequisite evidence before clearing mapping and atomic state, while pure numeric event witnesses retain only their original deadline across travel for the travel-end scan; no UObject is accessed or retained and F8/F7 remains a fresh resynchronization
runtime_task_class_mapping.save_merge_policy: a valid single-owner full F7 snapshot records the exact COMPLETE_CNT baseline for every requested catalog ID; an absent ID is baseline zero only for that valid query, while invalid or ambiguous ownership leaves the baseline unknown. An unresolved exact witness queues no SQL when its baseline is unknown. Otherwise it may request one immediate exact-ID confirmation and at most two retries spaced 15 seconds apart on the existing single below-normal worker; only strict count growth above the baseline confirms completion. Confirmations skip treasure SQL and are never periodic, and asynchronous results cannot erase newer exact or generic runtime completion evidence
runtime_task_class_mapping.delayed_result_atlas_policy: a result arriving after expanded-map attachment rebuilds immediately only when the exact retained layer is visibly open; a hidden or detached layer is retired and deferred until the next exact SetWorldMapImage edge

runtime_quest_event_witness.hook_kind: native pre-callback with reflected Locals parameters
runtime_quest_event_witness.event_filter: IsDynamic=true and QuestID is one exact entry in the 147-task catalog
runtime_quest_event_witness.arming_policy: IsDynamic must be true and QuestID must be one exact entry in the 147-task catalog. That exact event arms the numeric witness without a prior PROGRESS requirement, but the event itself is never completion.
runtime_quest_event_witness.additional_exact_sources: OnQuestBlueprintEndPlay and OnRenewQuestBlueprintEndPlay may arm only when the supplied task Actor class maps unambiguously through the complete 147-entry task-class table
runtime_quest_event_witness.witness_scope: per catalog task in one deduplicated fixed 147-entry numeric queue
runtime_quest_event_witness.coalescing_policy: each due witness queries only its exact catalog ID; all witnesses share the one-query-per-engine-tick budget, while repeated events for an already-live task do not extend its deadline or append a duplicate queue entry
runtime_quest_event_witness.completion_policy: final END proves the exact witnessed task complete even if its previous published state was NONE, FAIL, ACCEPTABLE, or PROGRESS; NONE alone is not completion and unwitnessed END remains fail closed; after completion, current NONE or END is only the inactive boundary for later repeatable reactivation
runtime_quest_event_witness.retention: numeric catalog index, boolean witness, steady-clock deadline, next 750 ms probe time, and one-byte probe count only; F8/F7 clears them; no event parameter, world context, task actor, or other UObject is retained
runtime_quest_event_witness.failure_policy: unknown IDs, non-dynamic events, invalid reflected schema, unverified final state, or an unknown F7 COMPLETE_CNT baseline cannot latch completion or queue confirmation SQL. With a known baseline, an expired exact witness may queue one fixed-bit exact-ID confirmation due immediately with at most two retries spaced 15 seconds apart; only strict count growth is accepted. Equal, lower, ambiguous, mismatched, unavailable, or failed results change no state. Three non-confirming attempts lock that task generation against repeated event rearming until a new F7 or current NONE or END followed by later ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS; the bound never becomes periodic SQL

visibility_hub.implementation: SG-12 keeps restrained blue-gray translucent cards and square Radar/Map checks. The fixed header is 98 reference units and footer 58; the intervening four-card body scrolls on short displays. Minimum supported viewport is 640x360. At 720p the main controls keep reference size; 21:9 adds side margins without stretching. While open, viewport/DPI checks run every 250 ms and update the retained tree without texture reimports, preserving settings and scroll position. Resize cancels pending confirmations before changing geometry. Invalid dimensions follow normal final-setting sampling and close. Numeric layout tests cover 83 cases; game input/composition remains unverified.
visibility_hub.text_vertical_centering: Source lifecycle centering covers initial open, language changes, status changes, and popup visibility changes. An exact-font TextBlock accepts GetDesiredSize only when ReturnValue has the same known Vector2D struct identity as the validated viewport-size return, then shrinks to the measured line height around its authored vertical center. Render-scale fallback retains its authored slot geometry and uses the existing pivot instead of desired-size recentering. Unavailable, mismatched, faulting, non-finite, non-positive, or oversized evidence preserves authored geometry. Reflow is edge-only and changes no per-frame path, radar or world-map geometry, or checkbox/button hit region. Live F6 visual acceptance remains NOT_VALIDATED.
visibility_hub.mini_game_scope: Fly, Mole, and Wave share one presentation category
visibility_hub.bird_egg_scope: Bird_Egg01_C and Bird_Egg02_C share one compact-only category; the world-map control is unavailable
visibility_hub.height_arrow_controls: Five independent compact-radar controls: Treasure, Area Quest, Mini-games, Boss and Assault, all enabled on clean defaults while explicit existing choices are preserved. Treasure retains its nearest six-piece left pointer; The legacy mole key controls the nearest Fly/Mole/Wave below-icon triangle; Area Quest controls each visible task marker; Boss and Assault control every retained encounter marker. All compare against playerZ minus 150. Mini-game and Area Quest/Boss/Assault alignment uses the shared inclusive +/-500 interval. Area Quests select their unique nearest authored height band; encounters use finite single-point authored spawn Z with no extra monster-origin offset. Aligned encounters restore the original glyph; unknown encounters preserve it without claiming alignment. Boss/Assault/Area sizes are 35/30/25 with a shared 4-reference-unit visible frame/triangle core; encounter triangles reserve another 1-unit dark-green outline per side, all scaled by display/DPI. Switches hide no markers and mutate no gameplay state.
visibility_hub.language_control: AUTO (Game Language) is the first popup option, followed by eleven explicit game UI languages. AUTO stays persisted; each actual F6 opening and F7 activation samples the game language once. Manual choices remain authoritative until AUTO is selected. Invalid detection retains the last valid language, using English only before the first valid sample. The selector shows the resolved language and the popup highlights AUTO while following.
visibility_hub.font_control: All eleven languages use pinned regular-font raster resources for 44 main slots in three status states, twelve language-popup choices, hover help, confirmations and numeric glyphs. Shared roles keep equal reference sizes; all three footer actions use 13 reference units / 26 raster pixels. There are 53 F6 TGAs: 33 main pages, one popup, two endonym value images, eleven 640x7632 atlases and six skins. Required glyph coverage is 423 main, 750 tooltip and 250 confirmation codepoints. Main/popup sheets are 1520x1704. Successful import and brush readback precede native-text hiding; main-page fallback remains native regular text, while missing confirmation resources remain cancel-only. No per-frame font discovery or runtime font generation is added.
visibility_hub.mod_status_control: F6 remains available while Radar is Off, On or in Error. The header contains title/Close and language/status controls; Reset, Vote and Feedback live in the footer.
visibility_hub.bug_report_control: Feedback asks before opening the fixed mod 254 Posts URL; the player submits the report on Nexus.
visibility_hub.data_boundary: Three packed numeric presentation masks, two display modes, one five-bit height-arrow mask, Scene range/count/distance settings and one bounded language preference; no catalog, save, cooldown, quest-state, completion-latch or provider-schedule mutation.
visibility_hub.area_quest_mode: AVAILABLE preserves prerequisite-proven visibility; ALL displays catalog tasks not excluded by saved or exact runtime completion, while a current active repeatable cycle remains visible
visibility_hub.assault_mode: AVAILABLE preserves save readiness, the authored Assault time window, defeat state, and future cooldown; ALL displays all 40 static Assault records without those live filters, while actual completion/cooldown authority remains unchanged; Boss and area-quest selection are unchanged
visibility_hub.closed_state_policy: Closed UMG performs no UObject/reflection work. Without a retained Escape press, hooks are removed and native input service returns after an atomic ingress check. Only an already-consumed press tail can temporarily remain until release or focus cleanup. The owner may flush one pending Scene preference write; no configuration hot polling.
visibility_hub.apply_policy: Publish masks, filter modes, five height controls, Scene settings and language in one game-thread transaction on change; a global reset also publishes its explicit reset flag if values already match. Ordinary preference changes persist atomically; dragged Scene changes retain a 300 ms debounce. A global preset makes pending writes immediately due, while Esc/F6/Close sample final controls and flush pending values. Unchanged samples without pending work do not write. Only a real expanded-map visibility change can request its existing coalesced map rebuild.
visibility_hub.close_policy: When a confirmation is active, Esc cancels only that modal and keeps F6 open. Its held/repeat/release tail remains consumed. A second F6, forced page close or focus loss closes the whole page and clears pending confirmation without dispatching it; focus loss takes priority over Escape. Without a confirmation, Esc, Close and a second F6 sample final controls, including the slider's last drag value, then close F6 and flush changed settings. Null current-controller probes during close/cancel resolve the host owner, while actual controller replacement fails closed. Travel and teardown clear pending intent and weak records. Source/isolated input tests are separate from game acceptance.
visibility_hub.escape_input_policy: F6 opens only after verifying the foreground UnrealWindow, current-process ownership and nonzero thread, then installing hooks on that one local window thread. WH_GETMESSAGE changes owned-window/child Escape key, repeat, release and character messages to WM_NULL before TranslateMessage/DispatchMessage; WH_CALLWNDPROC only observes owner focus, activation and destruction. The consumed press remains owned after UMG closes through key-up; the next independent press resumes normal routing. Synchronous focus loss requests full close and clears the held gesture while retaining protection until actual UMG removal. Travel, owner destruction and teardown clear state; process shutdown disables ingress without Unreal access. Hook failure rejects opening with failure 40. No global/low-level keyboard hook, synthetic input, UObject call or object scan occurs in this module. Other keys and other windows remain outside the filter scope.
visibility_hub.cursor_policy: set Game-and-UI mode before showing the cursor; during open-only 50 ms service reassert only after observing that gameplay hid it
visibility_hub.config_schema: Startup-only config/visibility.ini, at most 4096 bytes. Current serialization/public defaults contain six complete sections: [radar], [map], [scene], [modes], [height_arrows], [interface]. Scene treasure, area_quests and mini_games default true; range_meters=600 (0..1000), marker_limit=24 (0..50), distance_mode=nearest_center (off/central_radius/nearest_center/all). Either zero numeric setting suppresses Scene; distance off suppresses labels only. All five height keys treasure/area_quests/mole/boss/assault default true. Interface language defaults auto and remains persisted. The reader preserves strict legacy packed schema 1-4 and old three/five-section files; absent new fields use defaults while existing explicit choices survive. A present legacy Scene section still requires its original treasure and area_quests keys. Unknown, duplicate, malformed or incomplete required legacy input fails closed. No hot polling; F6 never rewrites hotkeys.ini.
visibility_hub.config_read_policy: once during native startup; no hot polling; duplicate, mixed-format, unknown, incomplete, malformed, or inconsistent-line-ending input falls back to safe defaults
visibility_hub.config_write_policy: Current six-section readable format; real option changes use temporary-file atomic replacement, with a 300 ms debounce for Scene range/count/distance changes and a pending-write flush on close.
visibility_hub.deployment_policy: preserve an existing user config file
visibility_hub.tooltip_policy: Native UWidget:SetToolTip manages 32 short help topics across 56 owners in the bounded 64-record pool. Eleven shared 640x7632 atlases contain 32 help, seven confirmation and fourteen numeric/symbol tiles each, totaling 583 tiles. Language edges replace the atlas; steady hover does not import or discover resources. Confirmation crops and numeric crops share the same regular-font pixels. Resize updates retained tooltip geometry as well as the page. Missing confirmation resources disable Yes; close/travel clear weak ownership.
visibility_hub.skin_policy: SG-12 keeps restrained blue-gray translucent cards and square Radar/Map checks. The fixed header is 98 reference units and footer 58; the intervening four-card body scrolls on short displays. Minimum supported viewport is 640x360. At 720p the main controls keep reference size; 21:9 adds side margins without stretching. While open, viewport/DPI checks run every 250 ms and update the retained tree without texture reimports, preserving settings and scroll position. Resize cancels pending confirmations before changing geometry. Invalid dimensions follow normal final-setting sampling and close. Numeric layout tests cover 83 cases; game input/composition remains unverified.
visibility_hub.global_preset: Bottom-row Reset to Defaults first opens a Yes/No confirmation. Only confirmed Yes restores all legal Radar/Map/Scene categories on, all five height choices on, both filters to Available, Scene 600 m/24/Aim and language AUTO. No or Esc closes only the confirmation with unchanged source settings. Confirmed restoration uses normal final-control sampling and one atomic global_reset_requested result; pending Scene writes flush even if values already match, while unchanged controls with no pending writes cause no write. Radar running state, startup hotkeys, saves and gameplay state are unchanged.
visibility_hub.scene_preview_policy: F6-owned cursor preview is limited to the settings Hub actually owning its input mode and the native HUD remaining visible. Scene may preview current settings while that owned menu is open; the existing enable, readiness, world/travel, activity, native-menu and HUD guards remain authoritative. Other cursor ownership never grants this exception. Scene creates no new input hook.
visibility_hub.endorse_control: The internal Endorse command opens the mod page after confirmation. Visible wording is Vote for This Mod, referring to Mod of the Month voting. The player completes the action on Nexus.
visibility_hub.confirmation_contract: Reset to Defaults, Vote for This Mod and Feedback each ask one localized question. Yes consumes the armed intent once before resetting display preferences or opening the fixed Nexus home/Posts URL. No or Esc cancels only the modal; focus loss closes the whole page. Background input remains blocked through dismissal and resize. Voting means Mod of the Month voting, distinct from endorsement; opening the mod page never submits a vote or feedback.
visibility_hub.language_simplification: SG-12 standardizes regular fonts and concise wording in all eleven languages. Reset to Defaults, Vote for This Mod and Feedback share a fixed footer. The 760x852 reference panel scrolls its four-card body on short displays and reflows the retained tree after viewport/DPI changes. Scene uses current-frame calibrated projection with native fallback, changed subpixel translations and visibility hysteresis. Existing catalogs, height rules, distance corrections and display defaults remain. Local deployment is authorized; release packages are deferred until owner testing.
visibility_hub.sg12_h1_opening_fix: SG-12-H1 fixes F6 failing to open in deployed SG-12. The two reflected UScrollBox parameter names are corrected to NewOrientation and NewScrollBarVisibility; type, offset and size checks remain. Two negative source checks cover these names, bringing the Hub regression suite from six to eight. All 61 UI files match SG-12 byte-for-byte.
